label: Formulated the Andean critique of colonialism as an inverted world demanding Pachakuti
description: Guaman Poma synthesized Quechua cosmic geography with moral theology, demonstrating that Spanish colonial extractivism destroyed Ayni (reciprocity) and created an inverted world ('el mundo al revés') that requires a cosmic and political Pachakuti to restore justice.
historicalContext: Composed in the Viceroyalty of Peru between 1584 and 1615, amidst the devastation of Andean population and forced silver mining at Potosí.
dialecticalTension: Confronts Spanish imperial claims of civilizing mission with the catastrophic destruction of Andean ethical civilization.

citations.author: Felipe Guaman Poma de Ayala
citations.work: El primer nueva corónica y buen gobierno
citations.quote: And so there is no remedy, for the poor Indians are destroyed, and the whole world is turned upside down.

citations.author: Rolena Adorno
citations.work: Guaman Poma: Writing and Resistance in Colonial Peru

label: Provided the foundational paradigm of early Latin American decolonial critique
description: Enrique Dussel identifies Guaman Poma as the seminal pioneer of liberation philosophy, who performed the first systemic critique of modernity from the underside of coloniality, articulating the exteriority of the conquered victim.
historicalContext: The genesis of the Philosophy of Liberation in 1970s Latin America.
dialecticalTension: Transforms Eurocentric historiography by centering the epistemic perspective of the colonized indigenous Andean.

citations.author: Enrique Dussel
citations.work: The Invention of the Americas: Eclipse of 'the Other' and the Myth of Modernity
citations.sectionOrPage: Chapter 4: The Conquest of the Other
citations.quote: Guaman Poma is the great indigenous philosopher who, from the underside of modernity, exposed the systemic myth of the conquest.

citations.author: Walter D. Mignolo
citations.work: The Darker Side of the Renaissance: Literacy, Territoriality, and Colonization

label: Prefigured the analysis of the coloniality of power and racialized labor
description: Aníbal Quijano rooted his theory of the Coloniality of Power directly in Guaman Poma's historical chronicle, which meticulously documented how Spanish rule instituted a global racial hierarchy to structure slave and tributary labor.
historicalContext: Peruvian sociology and the Modernity/Coloniality research program in Lima in the 1990s.
dialecticalTension: Demonstrates that racial classification is not an accidental byproduct of colonialism, but the foundational structural matrix of global capitalism.

citations.author: Aníbal Quijano
citations.work: Coloniality of Power, Eurocentrism, and Latin America
